title: The Burning Salt Again
premise: Lena Ishikawa has spent seven years hiding in the valley of Saltmere, where the salt in the earth deadens magic and keeps her safe from the mistress she fled. When a mute child arrives speaking a pre-kingdom tongue, Lena realizes the girl is a soul-vessel: her original self was sold to the court beneath the mountain, and unless it is reclaimed before the winter solstice, the child will hollow out entirely. Tracking the debt to its source, Lena discovers her former mistress brokered the sale—and that Lena's own name is written in the ledger as collateral. To save the child, Lena must surrender the invisibility she treasured, confront the woman who made her, and pay an inheritance she never knew was hers: the valley's protection itself, which only a blood-descendant of Saltmere's founders can release.
about_author: Dominic Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal mining towns before turning to fiction. They write about people who inherit debts they never agreed to, and who choose each other anyway.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A quiet morning gathering salt-thistle establishes her careful, invisible life in Saltmere and the rules that keep magic out. She tends her hedge-witch mentor Maren's grave and counts her small stores. Emotional beat: contentment built on fear, shown through ritual and routine.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A child appears at her door, barefoot in first snow, humming a melody that makes the salt lamps gutter. The girl cannot speak any living language but writes spirals in spilled salt. Emotional beat: dread breaking through domesticity; Lena recognizes magic has crossed a line it shouldn't.

chapters.title: What the Salt Won't Hold
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Testing the child with valley charms, Lena finds every ward slides off her like water. In Maren's buried papers she finds a sketch matching the girl's spiral sigil—labeled 'vessel.' Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried; first hint Maren knew more than she taught.

chapters.title: The Language Before Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the child (rendered in sensory fragments). Inside the girl's hollowed mind we glimpse flashes of the court beneath the mountain—cold halls, a ledger, hands taking something bright from her chest. Emotional beat: terror and longing; the reader learns what Lena can only guess.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Deciphering Maren's hidden accounts, Lena discovers soul-brokerage records and her own name listed as 'collateral, held.' The sale of the child's soul was brokered by someone using Maren's seal—after her death. Emotional beat: betrayal; the mentor-worship cracks.

chapters.title: Neighbors with Lanterns
chapters.summary: Village elder Tam Voss's POV. The valley council notices the wards fraying and blames the stranger-child. Tam, who remembers Lena's arrival years ago, quietly warns her to send the girl away before the valley turns on them both. Emotional beat: belonging revealed as conditional; kindness with a knife in it.

chapters.title: The Road Out Is the Road In
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena decides to leave the valley for the first time, taking the child north toward the mountain. Crossing the salt-line, magic floods back into the world—and into Lena, awakening abilities she suppressed for seven years. Emotional beat: vertigo and exhilaration; survival skills becoming weapons.

chapters.title: Ink and Ashes
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In a border town, a charm-seller recognizes the child's sigil and names the broker: Seraquine, a court factor who trades under many seals—including, once, Maren's. Lena buys passage with a charm she swore never to use again. Emotional beat: complicity; every step costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the child. At an inn, other hollowed vessels—adults, empty-eyed—are kept as laborers by a debtor caravan. The child's fragments show Lena what full hollowness looks like. Emotional beat: horror as prophecy; the stakes become flesh.

chapters.title: Seraquine
chapters.summary: Seraquine's POV. The elegant, weary factor reviews her ledger: the child's soul was purchased on behalf of the court beneath the mountain, but the true buyer's name is sealed even from her. She notes Lena's approach with professional interest—and recognition of Maren's hand in her training. Emotional beat: antagonist as mirror; both women shaped by the same teacher.

chapters.title: Bargaining Weather
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Seraquine offers Lena a trade: the child's soul for Lena's own name in the ledger, freeing Maren's estate but binding Lena to the court. Lena refuses—but learns the solstice deadline is real and closer than she thought. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy; refusal as commitment.

chapters.title: What My Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following Maren's final cipher, Lena finds a letter revealing Maren was herself a runaway vessel who bought back her own soul at terrible interest—and that the valley's protective salt was raised by Lena's bloodline, not Maren's. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined; the hiding place was always hers.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the child. As they near the mountain, the court's presence strengthens; the child begins speaking her old language fluently in her sleep, narrating the court's hunger. Lena understands the vessel is being 'called home.' Emotional beat: intimacy and estrangement; the girl she's protecting is slipping away.

chapters.title: Tollgate of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Tam Voss's POV. Back in Saltmere, the council votes to formally expel Lena and destroy Maren's cottage. Tam burns the decree instead and sets out after them—an old man carrying a lantern and a debt of his own. Emotional beat: redemption deferred; belonging chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena and the child enter the mountain through a drowned mine-shaft, navigating courts of minor creditors—things that trade in memories, shadows, first words. Each toll takes a memory from Lena. Emotional beat: escalating sacrifice; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the archive at the mountain's heart, Lena finds the master ledger and her own page: not collateral, but heir—the valley's founding covenant signed away by an ancestor to buy the family's survival. The court has been collecting interest for two hundred years. Emotional beat: revelation; her whole life reframed as a payment plan.

chapters.title: Audience with the Sealed Name
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs converging. The court's sovereign—a chorus of every soul it holds, including echoes of the hollowed—offers Lena the child's soul in exchange for releasing the valley's salt, opening her people to the court's reach. Emotional beat: climax of temptation; saving one means endangering everyone.

chapters.title: Solstice
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the longest night, Lena refuses both options and instead invokes the founding covenant's forgotten clause: a founder may assume the debt personally. She signs her name over the valley's, offering her own soul as surety while keeping the salt intact. Emotional beat: courage as bookkeeping; the bravest act is a signature.

chapters.title: Interest Due
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the child. The court begins extracting Lena's soul; the child, half-restored, does the unthinkable—she gives back a piece of her returned self to anchor Lena, singing the pre-kingdom word for 'belong.' Tam arrives with lantern raised, adding his small light. Emotional beat: love as leverage against an ancient machine.

chapters.title: The Renegotiation
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Anchored by the child's gift, Lena argues the contract before the chorus: a soul freely shared cannot be wholly owned. The court, bound by its own laws, must accept partial payment—Lena's memories of the valley, surrendered forever, in place of her whole self. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory; winning by losing precisely.

chapters.title: Salt and Snow
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They climb out into dawn. Lena no longer remembers why the valley mattered—only that the child crying beside her matters now. Tam leads them home to a village that, seeing the child restored, chooses to make room. Emotional beat: grief and grace entangled; a new family assembled from wreckage.

chapters.title: The Burning Salt Again
chapters.summary: Epilogue, the child's POV, now named Nell and beginning to speak. One year later, Nell teaches Lena words from before kingdoms while Lena teaches her hedge-craft without hiding. In the ledger-room far below, a new line waits beside Lena's name—not a debt, but a date. Emotional beat: belonging earned, inheritance transformed, and a future that will demand more.
